title: Who Showed Up
narrativeQuestion: When workers stopped the trains between 1877 and 1894, who showed up to make them move again, and how did the instrument of force change?

chapters.title: The Week
chapters.claim: In the same seven-day window that Grover Cleveland signed Labor Day into federal law, his administration moved toward breaking the Pullman boycott.

chapters.title: Martinsburg
chapters.claim: Local militia proved unreliable when the people under arms were neighbors of the strikers, prompting the first federal troop deployment in an American labor dispute.

chapters.title: Fourteen Days
chapters.claim: The Great Railroad Strike spread through the geometry of the rail and telegraph network rather than through a single national command structure.

chapters.title: Pittsburgh
chapters.claim: When Pittsburgh's own militia would not act, Pennsylvania imported troops from Philadelphia; the immediate tactical workaround helped produce a much larger catastrophe.

chapters.title: What 1877 Settled
chapters.claim: The strike produced no durable worker victory, but it did establish a repeatable method in which force could be moved away from local loyalties and toward state and federal authority.

chapters.title: Eight Hours
chapters.claim: The eight-hour demand was a fight over the measurable amount of life left after work, travel, sleep, and meals consumed the day.

chapters.title: Haymarket
chapters.claim: An unidentified bomb and a burst of police gunfire transformed a peaceful, thinning meeting into a mass-casualty event whose central factual uncertainty was never resolved.

chapters.title: Eight Men, One Bomb
chapters.claim: The Haymarket prosecution did not claim the defendants threw the bomb; sorting the record shows that location, proven conduct, and sentence do not align.

chapters.title: November, and Six Years Later
chapters.claim: Executions in 1887 and Altgeld's 1893 pardon exposed how much the Haymarket verdict outlived the evidence and how thoroughly association with the bombing damaged organized labor.

chapters.title: Fort Frick
chapters.claim: At Homestead, armed force was first procured through a private business chain before state troops entered the dispute.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours on the Monongahela
chapters.claim: Homestead workers defeated the Pinkertons at the landing but could not defeat the state militia that reopened the mill under armed protection six days later.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic at Pullman
chapters.claim: Because Pullman's company set both wages and many essential living costs, a wage cut without a rent cut transferred pressure through the entire household ledger.

chapters.title: The Piece of Paper
chapters.claim: The Pullman boycott demonstrated that a federal injunction could reach a national union faster and more comprehensively than troops could reach each strike site.

chapters.title: The Ladder
chapters.claim: Across seventeen years the machinery used against large strikes became less local, faster, more scalable, and increasingly legal in form.

chapters.title: Ten Words You Already Met
chapters.claim: Labor vocabulary becomes durable when each term is attached to the moment where it operated in the story.

chapters.title: Check What You Wrote Down
chapters.claim: The note-repair board corrects six common distortions by pointing students back to the evidence they just encountered.

accuracyNotes: Anchor the Great Railroad Strike chronology on the July 16, 1877 B&O wage-cut effective date while acknowledging that accounts differ about the exact first walkout.
Use about one hundred for the 1877 national death toll while preserving the documented range of roughly one hundred to one hundred sixty in teacher/source notes only.
Use about forty deaths for Pittsburgh and at least ten for Reading, reflecting the content master's conservative treatment of disputed figures.
Attribute the conclusion that most Haymarket police deaths came from police gunfire to historian Paul Avrich rather than presenting it as an uncontested contemporaneous finding.
Do not identify the Haymarket bomb thrower. No one was ever tried for throwing the bomb.
Do not imply the Knights of Labor organized the Haymarket meeting or bombing; the lesson uses the backlash to explain organizational damage by association.
Use roughly eight thousand for the Homestead militia and three Pinkerton deaths, matching the content master's stated choices amid source disagreement.
Do not claim Pullman paid workers in scrip. The company paid cash and deducted rent before workers received the balance.
Treat the Pullman ledger figures as the Pullman workers' own statement as printed in the federal Strike Commission report, not as neutral measurements produced by the company.
Preserve the distinction between striking and contempt of court: Debs was jailed for violating the injunction, not simply for leading a strike.
Do not claim Labor Day was created to appease the Pullman strikers. The bill predated the boycott; the significance is the compression of the calendar.
The narrative's synthesis is a comparison of instruments and response systems, not a claim that every strike had identical causes or that government and employer actions were legally equivalent.
